audit.why: 51.91% over 655 games, matching MC_WR_TABLES.nasus.drmundo. No elo-tier language in either layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper is the declared focus of this entire entry — it is the focus field, the loading-screen line, the tracked cooldown and the subject of half the prose — yet neither layer states the one condition that governs it. It is described only as 'his sustain spike'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'At the end of the duration or on Recast, Dr. Mundo deals a burst of damage to nearby enemies. If the burst hit an enemy, he heals a percentage of the stored damage.' The heal is conditional on the burst landing. Heart Zapper's range is 325 — a small radius around Mundo. A Nasus who walks out before it expires or is recast denies the entire heal, including everything Mundo stored by tanking Nasus's own damage during the window. That inverts the advice: the answer to Heart Zapper is footwork, not Wither, and it is available from level 2 with no items. Telling the player to 'Wither him when it's down' actively wastes the counterplay, because standing next to him to Wither is what feeds the heal.
audit.corrected: Heart Zapper only heals if its burst catches someone. Step outside the radius before it pops and he stores your damage for nothing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is never mentioned in either layer, in a matchup where Nasus's relationship to it is unusually clean.
audit.why: Mundo's passive resists the first Immobilizing effect that hits him, dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and reduce the passive's cooldown. Nasus's kit contains no immobilizing effect at all — his kitFlags are autoReset, slow, zone and percentHealth, with no hardCC, knockup or silence anywhere. So Nasus can never pop that passive himself, which means it is always still loaded when his jungler arrives, and a gank that leads with its own CC is what spends it. The second half matters just as much: the cannister has to be walked to, and Wither is a move-speed slow, so Wither is the tool that denies the pickup.
audit.corrected: Nothing in your kit is an immobilize, so his passive is never spent by you — it is still up for your jungler's CC, and Wither is what keeps him off the cannister afterwards.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers treat Blunt Force Trauma as purely an auto-attack tool that Wither shuts off — content whys[5] and wants.you[1] both call it 'auto-reliant' and imply the attack-speed slow neuters it.
audit.why: That is half the ability. Riot's text: 'Active - Dr. Mundo slams his "medical" bag into an enemy, dealing additional damage based on his missing Health.' The active gets stronger the lower Mundo drops, and its cooldown falls to 6s at rank 5. The current framing tells a Nasus that a low Mundo is a finished Mundo, which is exactly backwards and is the likeliest way this matchup actually kills the player: he dives a Mundo at 20% expecting a free kill and eats a maximum-roll E plus a Maximum Dosage heal.
audit.corrected: Wither cuts the auto-reset half; the active half scales with his missing health, so a low Mundo hits harder, not softer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet reports sequencingCues: 0. breakdown.cooldowns gives no number for anything, and advises 'Dodge or sidestep it' for Infected Bonesaw.
audit.why: Two real numbers change how this lane is played. Heart Zapper is 17/16.5/16/15.5/15s against Nasus's Wither at 15/14/13/12/11s, so Nasus's answer comes back before Mundo's does at every rank — that is the whole reason the lane levels off. And Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4s at every rank, which makes 'dodge or sidestep it' misleading as a plan: you cannot outwait a 4-second cooldown, you simply accept the chip and last-hit through it, which is what the content layer correctly says elsewhere.
audit.corrected: Give the 17s vs 15s relationship, and say plainly that Bonesaw at 4s flat is not something you wait out.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[4].why is the same boilerplate used across this champion's other matchups — 'Fury of the Sands flips dives ... suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take' — while phases[4].side says Skill and content whys[4] says 'nobody dies, it's even'.
audit.why: The layers describe opposite outcomes for level 6. The content layer is right and unusually well-reasoned here: Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percentage of missing health and then regenerates more over a long duration, so a Nasus all-in at 6 does not convert regardless of how well it goes. Calling it a flip contradicts both the side field printed beside it and the content layer's own text.
audit.corrected: Rewrite as the stalemate it is: neither ult kills the other, both let you keep farming.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers carry different level charts. full phases sides are [Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Skill, Nasus, Nasus]; content win is [Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Dr. Mundo, Skill, Skill, Skill, Nasus]. They disagree at stage 3 and stage 5.
audit.why: I am not proposing a side change here and want to be explicit about why. Unlike the Darius entry, neither full-layer why text contradicts its own side field in this matchup, so there is no internally-verifiable error to fix — only two editorial opinions about when the lane levels off. Picking one would be me inventing a power shift. This needs the owner to decide which array the front end reads.
audit.corrected: No edit proposed. Flagged for the owner to reconcile.

audit.why: Checked the packet's suspectNames flag for 'His Maximum Dosage' in spikes[1].text. It is a false positive — Maximum Dosage is Dr. Mundo's real R name per the kit file. No name change needed. The content layer's ability naming in this matchup is accurate throughout, including Infected Bonesaw, Heart Zapper, Spirit Fire, Fury of the Sands and Soul Eater.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain spike. Wither him when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Dr. Mundo Infected Bonesaw: Throws a cleaver that slows and deals %current-HP magic damage; refunds HP. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — 17s at rank 1 against your 15s Wither, so your answer lands first. It heals him only if the burst catches someone, so leave the radius before it pops. - Dr. Mundo Infected Bonesaw: 4s flat. You cannot outwait it.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Heart Zapper: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade around Heart Zapper by footwork: step out before the burst and he heals none of what he stored. Then commit. If ahead, freeze and starve him.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands flips dives: pop R, Wither Dr. Mundo, and suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take.
edits.after: Level 6 is a stalemate, not a swing: Maximum Dosage heals back whatever you commit, and Fury of the Sands just lets you farm through his return.

edits.before: His sustain spike. Wither him when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His sustain spike — but the heal needs the burst to land. Leave the radius before it pops.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Blunt Force Trauma scales off his missing health — a low Mundo hits harder.

edits.before: Your engage is premium gank setup — ping your jungler when Heart Zapper is down. Ward river before extended trades.
edits.after: You own no immobilise, so his passive is still loaded — let your jungler's CC spend it, then Wither him off the cannister.

edits.before: Wither him in every extended fight to gut his attack speed and the auto-damage half of his E
edits.after: Step out of Heart Zapper's radius before it bursts — no hit means he heals none of it

edits.before: Sheen/Iceborn gives your stacked Q real burst and Wither's attack-speed slow guts his auto-reliant E — the trade math finally balances.
edits.after: Sheen/Iceborn gives your stacked Q real burst and Wither craters his attack speed — but his E active grows as his own health drops.

notes:
This is one of the better-written entries in the slice — the content layer names abilities correctly throughout and its level-6 read ('nobody dies, it's even') is more accurate than the full layer's boilerplate. Most of my work here was adding the two mechanics that decide the matchup rather than fixing errors.

The packet's suspectNames hit on 'His Maximum Dosage' is a FALSE POSITIVE — that is Mundo's real R name. Worth tuning the detector; it fired on four of my nine matchups and was wrong every time (also 'Spirit Fire's', 'No Wither', 'Soak Siphoning Strike', 'His Collateral Damage' — all correct names, flagged only because of the adjacent word).

One claim I could NOT verify and therefore did not touch: both layers state that Mundo's passive 'refunds the cost' of Infected Bonesaw (content early, whys[0], wants.foe[0]) and breakdown.cooldowns says the cleaver 'refunds HP'. The kit file's Q description mentions no health cost and no refund, and the passive text covers CC resistance, the cannister and increased health regeneration — not a per-cast refund. The claim may well be right in game, but it is not derivable from the files on disk and the brief forbids asserting it from the web, so I left every instance alone rather than half-correct it. Someone with Wiki access should settle whether the refund is on the passive, on Q itself, or neither.

I did not propose a level-chart side change here, unlike Darius. The two layers disagree at stages 3 and 5, but in this matchup no full-layer why text contradicts its own side field, so there was no internally-verifiable error — only two editorial opinions. Choosing between them would have meant inventing a power shift.
